```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))

import polars as pl
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

import helpers as H
import diary as D
import plots as P
import spec as S

# Fail the render fast if the environment is broken (drives unmapped, vendor run
# missing, crosswalk / bridge / spec assumptions violated, ...).
checks = H.run_all_checks()
assert checks["ok"].all(), "Sanity checks failed:\n" + str(checks.filter(~pl.col("ok")))

# Single weight basis: the vendor-weights pipeline run, which uses the same vendor
# weights the legacy scripts consume. (The new pipeline's own raked weighting is
# intentionally out of scope here — this report is structural.)
BASIS = "vendor"
LEG_C, NEW_C = P.LEG_C, P.NEW_C

legacy = H.load_legacy_daysim()
new = H.load_new_daysim(BASIS)
new_days = H.new_days_with_dow(BASIS)

# Common universe: households in both, persons with >=1 Tue-Thu day in both.
hhnos = H.common_households(legacy["hh"], new["hh"])
persons = H.common_persons(legacy["personday"], new_days, hhnos)

# Universe-restricted per-table frames, keyed by the report's table names, for
# uniform access in the coverage and distribution sections.
LEG = {
    "hh": legacy["hh"].filter(pl.col("hhno").is_in(hhnos)),
    "person": H.filter_universe(legacy["person"], persons),
    "personday": H.filter_universe(legacy["personday"], persons),
    "tour": H.filter_universe(legacy["tour"], persons),
    "trip": H.filter_universe(legacy["trip"], persons),
}
NEW = {
    "hh": new["hh"].filter(pl.col("hhno").is_in(hhnos)),
    "person": H.filter_universe(new["person"], persons),
    "personday": H.filter_universe(new_days.drop("day").rename({"dow": "day"}), persons),
    "tour": H.filter_universe(new["tour"], persons),
    "trip": H.filter_universe(new["trip"], persons),
}

leg_trips, leg_tours, leg_pdays = LEG["trip"], LEG["tour"], LEG["personday"]
new_trips, new_tours, new_pdays = NEW["trip"], NEW["tour"], NEW["personday"]

# Intersection of weighted-eligible person-days: an identical day universe on both
# sides (legacy drops zero-weight days; the new pipeline keeps them).
common_days = (
    leg_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") > 0).select(["hhno", "pno", "day"])
    .join(
        new_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") > 0).select(["hhno", "pno", "day"]),
        on=["hhno", "pno", "day"], how="inner",
    )
)


def on_common_days(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return df.join(common_days, on=["hhno", "pno", "day"], how="semi")


def show(df: pl.DataFrame, floatfmt: str = ",.1f") -> None:
    display(Markdown(
        df.to_pandas().to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=floatfmt, intfmt=",")
    ))


# Record-level matchers (tours on anchor times, trips through the linked-group bridge)
# carry every column through, so any column can be compared record-to-record.
mt_tours = H.matched_tours(leg_tours, new_tours)
mt_trips = H.matched_trips(leg_trips, new_trips, basis=BASIS)

# Zone bridges: legacy TAZ1454 vs the new pipeline's TM2 zones, compared on TAZ1454.
TAZ = {
    "hh": {"hhtaz": H.taz1454("hh", "hhtaz", BASIS)},
    "person": {"pwtaz": H.taz1454("person", "pwtaz", BASIS),
               "pstaz": H.taz1454("person", "pstaz", BASIS)},
}
# Trip column agreement is measured on trips both pipelines linked identically
# (matched_exact) -- "given the same input trips, do the outputs agree?". Trips linked
# differently (matched_partial) are a linking divergence, reported in @sec-matched-trips.
MATCHED = {
    "tour": mt_tours["matched"],
    "trip": mt_trips["matched"].filter(pl.col("match_status") == "matched_exact"),
}


def comparable_cols(table: str) -> set[str]:
    return {
        cs.name for cs in S.columns(table)
        if S.comparability(cs, LEG[table], NEW[table]) == S.COMPARABLE
    }


def coverage(table: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return S.coverage_table(
        table, LEG[table], NEW[table],
        matched=MATCHED.get(table), taz_bridges=TAZ.get(table),
    )


# Paired (legacy value vs new value) frames for the coordinate scatter panels:
# hh/person/person-day join directly on their keys; tours/trips use the matched frame.
def paired_frame(table: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    if table in MATCHED:
        return MATCHED[table]
    keys = S.KEYS[table]
    return LEG[table].join(NEW[table], on=keys, how="inner", suffix="_new")


PAIRED = {t: paired_frame(t) for t in ["hh", "person", "personday", "tour", "trip"]}


# Inner-tabset structure for the column-by-column section: (tab title, kinds).
# Coordinates and Weights render as legacy-vs-new scatters (agreement on the diagonal);
# the rest are distribution comparisons.
KIND_TABS = [
    ("Categorical", [S.Kind.CATEGORICAL]),
    ("Counts", [S.Kind.COUNT]),
    ("Times", [S.Kind.TIME]),
    ("Continuous", [S.Kind.CONTINUOUS]),
    ("Coordinates", [S.Kind.COORD]),
    ("Weights", [S.Kind.WEIGHT]),
]


def emit_kind_tabsets(table: str) -> None:
    """Emit a Quarto inner tabset of one distribution grid per column kind."""
    comp = comparable_cols(table)
    display(Markdown("::: {.panel-tabset}\n"))
    for title, kinds in KIND_TABS:
        fig, n, flagged = P.kind_grid(
            table, kinds, LEG[table], NEW[table], comp, paired=PAIRED[table]
        )
        display(Markdown(f"### {title}\n"))
        if fig is None:
            display(Markdown("_No comparable columns of this kind._\n"))
            continue
        flag_note = f", {flagged} showing notable disagreement" if flagged else ""
        display(Markdown(f"{n} comparable column(s){flag_note}.\n"))
        display(HTML(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False)))
    display(Markdown(":::\n"))


def emit_coverage_tabsets() -> None:
    """Emit a Quarto tabset of the per-table spec coverage & agreement tables."""
    display(Markdown("::: {.panel-tabset}\n"))
    for table, title in [
        ("hh", "Households"), ("person", "Persons"), ("personday", "Person-days"),
        ("tour", "Tours"), ("trip", "Trips"),
    ]:
        display(Markdown(f"### {title}\n"))
        cov = coverage(table).select(
            ["column", "definition", "map", "legacy", "new", "n", "% agree", "note"]
        )
        show(cov, floatfmt=",.0f")
    # HouseholdDay: in the spec, emitted by neither pipeline.
    display(Markdown("### HouseholdDay\n"))
    hd = pl.DataFrame({"column": [cs.name for cs in S.columns("householdday")]})
    display(Markdown(
        "`HouseholdDayDaysimModel` is part of the DaySim spec but **emitted by "
        "neither pipeline** (joint-tour bookkeeping the survey does not support). "
        f"Its {hd.height} columns are listed for completeness:\n"
    ))
    show(hd)
    display(Markdown(":::\n"))


tour_match = mt_tours  # alias for the exec summary / matched-tours section
xwalk = H.build_crosswalk(BASIS)
```

## 2. The two pipelines {#sec-pipelines}

- **Legacy** — six sequential scripts, all logic in code:
  `00-preprocess → 01-taz_spatial_join → 02a-reformat → 02b-link_trips_week → 03a-tour_extract_week → 03b-assign_day`
- **New** — declarative steps over a canonical, schema-validated data model:
  `load_data → clean → imputation → link_trips → detect_joint_trips → extract_tours → [weighting] → add_zone_ids → format_daysim → write_data`
- For this validation the `[weighting]` slot is `add_existing_weights`, consuming
  the same vendor weights the legacy scripts use, so differences reflect processing
  logic, not weighting method.

## 3. Weighting: how each pipeline gets the person-day weight {#sec-weighting}

Both pipelines expand the survey with the **same vendor weights**, but they arrive at the
person-day weight (`pdexpfac`) two different ways. This one difference accounts for most of
the record-count and weighted differences reported later, so it is worth establishing up front.

- **New pipeline** — uses the vendor's `day_weight` column **as issued**.
- **Legacy** — does not read `day_weight`. Its `03b-assign_day` step **reconstructs** the
  weight from the person weight: `pdexpfac = person_weight / n_complete_weekdays`. (This
  report reproduces that formula exactly — 100% — from the raw columns, confirming the
  reading of the legacy code.)

Legacy's reconstruction is internally consistent and conserves each person's weight exactly.
The two approaches diverge on a narrower question: **which days count as eligible to carry
weight.** They read different completeness flags, and the survey provides both:

- `is_complete` — did **this person** complete their diary that day?
- `hh_day_complete` — did **the whole household** complete that day?

The vendor's weighting frame applies the **household-level** test; legacy's formula applies
the **person-level** one. Every person-day falls cleanly into one of three groups:

```{python}
#| label: weighting-groups

_lk = ["hhno", "pno", "day"]
_rd = H.load_raw("day").select(
    pl.col("hh_id").alias("hhno"), pl.col("person_num").alias("pno"),
    pl.col("travel_dow").alias("day"), "is_complete", "hh_day_complete", "day_weight",
)
_w = (
    leg_pdays.select(_lk + ["pdexpfac"]).rename({"pdexpfac": "leg_w"})
    .join(new_pdays.select(_lk + ["pdexpfac"]).rename({"pdexpfac": "new_w"}),
          on=_lk, how="full", coalesce=True)
    .with_columns(pl.col("leg_w").fill_null(-999), pl.col("new_w").fill_null(-999))
    .join(_rd, on=_lk, how="left")
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("leg_w") == -999).then(pl.lit("A"))
        .when((pl.col("leg_w") > 0) & (pl.col("new_w") <= 0)).then(pl.lit("B"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("C")).alias("grp")
    )
)
_gA = _w.filter(pl.col("grp") == "A")
_gB = _w.filter(pl.col("grp") == "B")
_gC = _w.filter(pl.col("grp") == "C")

# Each group is homogeneous on both flags (verified: min == max), so the labels are exact.
for _g, _isc, _hhc in [(_gA, 0, 0), (_gB, 1, 0), (_gC, 1, 1)]:
    assert _g["is_complete"].min() == _g["is_complete"].max() == _isc
    assert _g["hh_day_complete"].min() == _g["hh_day_complete"].max() == _hhc

groups = pl.DataFrame([
    {"group": "A", "person-days": _gA.height, "person's day complete": "no",
     "household's day complete": "no", "vendor day_weight": "0",
     "legacy pdexpfac": "day not emitted", "new pdexpfac": "0"},
    {"group": "B", "person-days": _gB.height, "person's day complete": "yes",
     "household's day complete": "no", "vendor day_weight": "0",
     "legacy pdexpfac": "> 0", "new pdexpfac": "0"},
    {"group": "C", "person-days": _gC.height, "person's day complete": "yes",
     "household's day complete": "yes", "vendor day_weight": "> 0",
     "legacy pdexpfac": "> 0", "new pdexpfac": "> 0"},
])
show(groups, floatfmt=",.0f")
```

**Groups A and C are agreement.** In A the person did not finish their diary: legacy drops
the day, the new pipeline keeps the row at weight 0 — the same treatment, expressed
differently. In C both pipelines weight the day.

**Group B is the divergence.** These are days where the person finished their diary but
someone else in their household did not. The vendor zeroes them; legacy, reading only the
person-level flag, weights them.

The consequence is not a difference in *totals* — it is a difference in *allocation*:

```{python}
#| label: weighting-allocation

_leg_total, _new_total = leg_pdays["pdexpfac"].sum(), new_pdays["pdexpfac"].sum()
_leg_on_C, _leg_on_B = _gC["leg_w"].sum(), _gB["leg_w"].sum()
_diluted = _gC.filter((pl.col("leg_w") - pl.col("new_w")).abs() >= 1e-6).height

alloc = pl.DataFrame([
    {"measure": "person-days carrying a positive weight",
     "legacy": float(leg_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") > 0).height),
     "new": float(new_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") > 0).height)},
    {"measure": "total weighted person-days", "legacy": _leg_total, "new": _new_total},
    {"measure": "  ...on group C days (both weight)", "legacy": _leg_on_C, "new": _new_total},
    {"measure": "  ...on group B days (vendor zeroed)", "legacy": _leg_on_B, "new": 0.0},
])
show(alloc, floatfmt=",.0f")

display(Markdown(f"""
Both pipelines expand to the **identical grand total of {_new_total:,.0f} weighted
person-days** — the person weight is fully conserved either way. They differ in where that
total lands: legacy places **{_leg_on_C / _leg_total * 100:.1f}%** of it on the days the
vendor's frame weights, and the remaining **{_leg_on_B / _leg_total * 100:.1f}%
({_leg_on_B:,.0f} weighted person-days)** on group B. Because each person's weight is
divided by a denominator that counts group B days, **{_diluted:,}** of the {_gC.height:,}
group C days also carry a slightly *lower* legacy weight than the vendor's.
"""))
```

Two things follow for the rest of this report. First, because the grand totals agree
exactly, no check of weighted *totals* can surface this — it is visible only per day, which
is why it surfaces here in the record counts (@sec-unweighted) and the `pdexpfac` column
(@sec-divergences). Second, the household-level rule lives in a separate `hh_day_complete`
column, not in the `is_complete` flag legacy reads; the vendor's issued `day_weight` is the
only place the rule is actually applied. The new pipeline reproduces the vendor's frame by
construction because it consumes `day_weight` directly rather than re-deriving it.

## 4. Methodology & joinability {#sec-methodology}

### The spec is the contract

The **DaySim pydantic models** (`src/data_canon/models/daysim.py`) define the output
columns, their types, bounds and value domains. Every column in this report is read
off those models — never hand-listed — and its value labels come from the codebook
enums (`src/data_canon/codebook/daysim.py`). Each column is classified from its field
metadata into a comparison strategy (categorical, count, time, continuous, coordinate,
zone, weight) that determines how it is compared and plotted.

### Record linkage, per table

| Table | How the two pipelines are matched |
|---|---|
| Households, Persons, Person-days | Join directly on the surviving IDs (`hhno` / `hhno,pno` / `hhno,pno,day`). |
| Tours | Numbered independently by each pipeline, so **matched on person-day + all three anchor times** (leave origin, arrive destination, return to origin). |
| Trips | Legacy `tsvid` and new `tsvid` are different id spaces, so trips are matched through a **linked-group bridge**: the raw-trip overlap of every legacy↔new linked-trip pair, keeping mutual-best pairs (@sec-matched-trips). |

### Normalisations applied before comparison

- **Time** — legacy writes HHMM clock integers; the new pipeline writes minutes past
  midnight (DaySim spec). Legacy is normalised to minutes so differences are
  arithmetic-safe.
- **Zones** — the DaySim `taz` fields carry TM2 `TAZ_NODE`; legacy carries TM1
  `TAZ1454`. Compared on `TAZ1454` via the new pipeline's survey outputs.
- **Legacy missing codes** — legacy writes `9` for "missing" in `hownrent`/`hrestype`
  where the spec uses `-1`; remapped so the two are comparable (without this the
  agreement was understated).
- **Drive-to-transit** — legacy emits two DaySim trip rows (auto access leg, then
  walk-transit leg) sharing one `tsvid`; the new pipeline emits one linked `mode=7`
  row. The legacy pair is collapsed to one linked trip before comparison.

Every column of every DaySim table, with whether each pipeline emits it, whether it is
comparable, and — where it is — the agreement rate. Columns disagreeing on more than
5% of records are flagged **⚠** and explained in @sec-divergences. Non-comparable
columns (a pipeline stub, absent on one side, or an independent id space) carry the
reason in the note column.

emit_coverage_tabsets()

### Directly-mapped attribute integrity {#sec-integrity}

Columns copied straight from a single survey field (marked **mapped** above) must agree
**1:1** — they involve no modeling. Below, agreement is computed only on rows where the
legacy value is a real value (excluding missing sentinels and values the new pipeline is
documented to impute, e.g. non-binary/missing gender). Anything short of 100% here is a
**suspected mapping discrepancy to investigate**, not expected imputation noise.

```{python}
#| label: mapping-integrity
#| echo: false

mi = pl.concat([
    S.mapping_integrity("hh", LEG["hh"], NEW["hh"]).with_columns(pl.lit("hh").alias("table")),
    S.mapping_integrity("person", LEG["person"], NEW["person"]).with_columns(pl.lit("person").alias("table")),
]).select(["table", "column", "definition", "n (legacy real value)", "% agree", "n disagree", "note"])
show(mi, floatfmt=",.0f")

dirty = mi.filter(~pl.col("clean") if "clean" in mi.columns else pl.col("n disagree") > 0)
n_dirty = mi.filter(pl.col("n disagree") > 0).height
if n_dirty:
    display(Markdown(
        f"⚠ **{n_dirty} mapped column(s) disagree on values legacy reports as real** — "
        "`hownrent` and `hrestype` flip a household's ownership / residence type on a small "
        "number of records with no missing-value or imputation explanation. This is a genuine "
        "discrepancy worth a root-cause look at the new pipeline's household field mapping "
        "(reported here, not yet fixed)."
    ))
else:
    display(Markdown("All directly-mapped attributes agree 1:1 on non-missing legacy values."))
```

## 6. Aggregate comparison — unweighted {#sec-unweighted}

### Record counts

Row counts for each table, legacy vs new, both counted on positive-weight records only
(`new*` excludes the zero-weight rows the new pipeline retains; legacy carries none).

The person-day `diff` is entirely the **group B** days of @sec-weighting — days the vendor
zeroed because the household did not complete them, which legacy's person-level completeness
test weights instead. It is a weighting-frame difference, not records the new pipeline failed
to produce. The zero-weighted column adds **group A** on top of those (person's diary
incomplete; legacy drops the row, the new pipeline keeps it at weight 0). Tour and trip gaps
run larger because they compound the same person-day difference with tour-detection and
tour-formatting differences (@sec-divergences).

```{python}
#| label: record-counts

def _nz(df, col):
    return df.filter(pl.col(col) > 0).height

def _zero(df, col):
    return df.filter(pl.col(col) <= 0).height

counts = pl.DataFrame([
    {"entity": "households",  "legacy": len(hhnos),        "new*": len(hhnos),                "zero-weighted records (new)": 0},
    {"entity": "persons",     "legacy": persons.height,    "new*": persons.height,            "zero-weighted records (new)": 0},
    {"entity": "person-days", "legacy": leg_pdays.height,  "new*": _nz(new_pdays, "pdexpfac"), "zero-weighted records (new)": _zero(new_pdays, "pdexpfac")},
    {"entity": "tours",       "legacy": leg_tours.height,  "new*": _nz(new_tours, "toexpfac"), "zero-weighted records (new)": _zero(new_tours, "toexpfac")},
    {"entity": "trips",       "legacy": leg_trips.height,  "new*": _nz(new_trips, "trexpfac"), "zero-weighted records (new)": _zero(new_trips, "trexpfac")},
]).with_columns(
    (pl.col("new*") - pl.col("legacy")).alias("diff"),
    ((pl.col("new*") - pl.col("legacy")) / pl.col("legacy") * 100)
    .map_elements(lambda v: f"{v:+.1f}%", return_dtype=pl.String).alias("diff %"),
).select("entity", "legacy", "new*", "diff", "diff %", "zero-weighted records (new)")
show(counts, floatfmt=",.0f")
```

*\*Count excludes zero-weight records; these are retained and recoverable in the new pipeline.*

### Trip structuring {#sec-structuring}

How raw trips become structured travel, stage by stage. The first three bars count
**linked trips** (unlinked → linked → surviving into tours); the fourth counts **tours**.
All four share one record axis. Legacy "trips in tours" is counted after collapsing its
drive-transit two-row split, so the unit matches the new pipeline on both sides.

```{python}
#| label: trip-structuring

xwalk_universe = H.filter_universe(
    on_common_days(xwalk.rename({"dow": "day"})).rename({"day": "dow"}), persons, day_col=None,
)
leg_trips_cd = on_common_days(leg_trips)
new_trips_cd = on_common_days(new_trips)
stages = H.trip_structuring_table(
    xwalk_universe, leg_trips_cd, new_trips_cd,
    on_common_days(leg_tours), on_common_days(new_tours),
)
show(stages.select(["stage", "unit", "legacy", "new",
                    "retention_legacy_pct", "retention_new_pct", "note"]), floatfmt=",.0f")
P.trip_structuring_fig(stages).show()

# New-side drops at tour formatting: tours must be VALID *and* COMPLETE.
lk = (
    H.load_new_survey("linked_trips", BASIS)
    .select(pl.col("hh_id").alias("hhno"), "person_id",
            pl.col("travel_dow").alias("day"), "tour_id")
    .join(H.load_new_survey("unlinked_trips", BASIS)
          .select(pl.col("hh_id").alias("hhno"), pl.col("person_num").alias("pno"),
                  "person_id").unique(), on=["hhno", "person_id"])
    .drop("person_id")
    .join(common_days, on=["hhno", "pno", "day"], how="semi")
    .join(H.load_new_survey("tours", BASIS).select("tour_id", "tour_data_quality", "tour_category"),
          on="tour_id", how="left")
)
QUALITY = {0: "Valid", 1: "Single-trip tour", 2: "Home-based loop",
           3: "No home anchor", 4: "Invalid (unknown)", 5: "Change-mode primary"}
CATEGORY = {1: "Complete (home→home)", 2: "Ends away", 3: "Starts away", 4: "Both ends away"}
drop_reasons = (
    lk.filter(~((pl.col("tour_data_quality") == 0) & (pl.col("tour_category") == 1)))
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("tour_data_quality") != 0)
        .then(pl.col("tour_data_quality").replace_strict(QUALITY, default="?"))
        .otherwise(pl.col("tour_category").replace_strict(CATEGORY, default="?"))
        .alias("new pipeline: trips dropped at tour formatting")
    )
    .group_by("new pipeline: trips dropped at tour formatting")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("trips")).sort("trips", descending=True)
)
show(drop_reasons, floatfmt=",.0f")
```

## 8. Household & person income {#sec-income}

`hhincome` is derived as a representative dollar value within the survey's detailed
income bracket, and the two pipelines pick different midpoints, so exact-dollar match
is meaningless. Binning back to the source brackets is the apples-to-apples test.

```{python}
#| label: income

_bin_idx = {lab: i for i, lab in enumerate(H.INCOME_BIN_LABELS)}
lb = LEG["hh"].with_columns(H.income_bin()).select("hhno", "income_bin")
nb = NEW["hh"].with_columns(H.income_bin()).select("hhno", pl.col("income_bin").alias("income_bin_new"))
ij = lb.join(nb, on="hhno", how="inner").drop_nulls().with_columns(
    (pl.col("income_bin_new").cast(pl.String).replace_strict(_bin_idx)
     - pl.col("income_bin").cast(pl.String).replace_strict(_bin_idx)).abs().alias("bin_dist")
)
inc_agree = 100 * ij.filter(pl.col("bin_dist") == 0).height / ij.height
inc_big_diff = ij.filter(pl.col("bin_dist") > 1).height
inc_exact = H.pct_match(LEG["hh"], NEW["hh"], ["hhno"], "hhincome")
inc_missing_imputed = LEG["hh"].filter(pl.col("hhincome") <= 0).join(
    NEW["hh"].filter(pl.col("hhincome") > 0).select("hhno"), on="hhno", how="semi").height

display(Markdown(
    f"- Same source income bracket **{inc_agree:.1f}%** of the time "
    f"({ij.height:,} households reporting income; only **{inc_big_diff}** differ by "
    f"more than one bracket).\n"
    f"- Exact-dollar match {inc_exact:.0f}% (different midpoints within a bracket).\n"
    f"- {inc_missing_imputed:,} households legacy leaves blank are imputed by the new pipeline."
))

leg_inc = LEG["hh"].with_columns(H.income_bin_index()).drop_nulls("inc_bin")
new_inc = NEW["hh"].with_columns(H.income_bin_index()).drop_nulls("inc_bin")
inc_dist = H.distribution_table(leg_inc, new_inc, "inc_bin", H.INCOME_BIN_NAMES)
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_bar(x=inc_dist["label"], y=inc_dist["legacy_pct"], name="Legacy", marker_color=LEG_C, opacity=0.85)
fig.add_bar(x=inc_dist["label"], y=inc_dist["new_pct"], name="New", marker_color=NEW_C, opacity=0.85)
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", template="plotly_white", height=340,
                  legend={"orientation": "h", "x": 0.4, "y": 1.1}, yaxis_title="% of households")
fig.show()
```

## 9. Person-day record-level agreement {#sec-personday}

Person-days join directly, so the tour and stop counters compare record by record. The
new pipeline populates only the aggregate counters (`hbtours`, `wbtours`, `uwtours`);

"""))

                    subplot_titles=("Tour purpose", "Tour mode"))

## 11. Matched trips {#sec-matched-trips}

Record-level trip comparison, new to this report. Each legacy linked trip is matched to
its new counterpart through the linked-group bridge; the match taxonomy accounts for
every trip on each side exactly once.

```{python}
#| label: trip-match

display(Markdown(f"""
| Match status | Trips |
|---|---|
| Matched — identical raw-trip sets (linkers agree) | {mt_trips['n_exact']:,} |
| Matched — overlapping sets (linking differs) | {mt_trips['n_partial']:,} |
| Legacy only (no new counterpart) | {mt_trips['n_legacy_only']:,} |
| New only (no legacy counterpart) | {mt_trips['n_new_only']:,} |
| Legacy drive-transit rows collapsed | {mt_trips['n_split_collapsed']:,} |

**{mt_trips['n_matched']:,}** of {mt_trips['n_legacy']:,} legacy trips matched
({mt_trips['match_rate_pct']:.1f}%). Purpose, mode, driver/passenger and path type
classification flow on matched trips:
"""))

fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, specs=[[{"type": "sankey"}, {"type": "sankey"}]],
                    subplot_titles=("Destination purpose", "Mode"))
fig.add_trace(P.confusion_sankey(matched_pairs := mt_trips["matched"], "dpurp", "dpurp_new",
                                 S.labels("trip", "dpurp")), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_trace(P.confusion_sankey(matched_pairs, "mode", "mode_new", S.labels("trip", "mode")), row=1, col=2)
fig.update_layout(height=520, margin={"t": 50, "b": 20})
fig.show()
```

On matched trips the clock times agree essentially exactly — **`deptm` 100%**, **`arrtm`
99.7%** — so a difference histogram would be a single spike at zero; the departure and
arrival distributions themselves are in the §6 Trips → Times grid. Only `endacttm` (the
destination activity-end time) differs, by ~15 min, an activity-end-convention difference
noted in @sec-divergences.

## 12. Weighted comparison (vendor weights) {#sec-weighted}

```{python}
#| label: weighted-totals

totals = pl.DataFrame([
    {"measure": "person-days (pdexpfac)", "legacy": leg_pdays["pdexpfac"].sum(),
     "new": new_pdays["pdexpfac"].sum()},
    {"measure": "trips (trexpfac)", "legacy": leg_trips["trexpfac"].sum(),
     "new": new_trips["trexpfac"].sum()},
    {"measure": "tours (toexpfac)", "legacy": leg_tours["toexpfac"].sum(),
     "new": new_tours["toexpfac"].sum()},
]).with_columns(
    ((pl.col("new") - pl.col("legacy")) / pl.col("legacy") * 100)
    .map_elements(lambda v: f"{v:+.2f}%", return_dtype=pl.String).alias("pct_diff")
)
show(totals, floatfmt=",.0f")

# Reconciliation: the extra zero-weight person-days new keeps carry zero-weight trips
# and tours, so they inflate record counts but contribute nothing to any weighted total.
zwd = new_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") <= 0).select(["hhno", "pno", "day"])
zw_trips = new_trips.join(zwd, on=["hhno", "pno", "day"], how="semi")
zw_tours = new_tours.join(zwd, on=["hhno", "pno", "day"], how="semi")
n_zero_pdays = zwd.height

wp = H.distribution_table(leg_trips, new_trips, "dpurp", S.labels("trip", "dpurp"),
                          weight_cols=("trexpfac", "trexpfac"))
wm = H.distribution_table(leg_trips, new_trips, "mode", S.labels("trip", "mode"),
                          weight_cols=("trexpfac", "trexpfac"))
display(Markdown(
    f"- **Weighted person-day totals agree exactly.** The "
    f"{n_zero_pdays:,} zero-weight person-days the new pipeline keeps "
    f"carry **{zw_trips.height:,} zero-weight trips** and **{zw_tours.height:,} zero-weight "
    f"tours** (all verified zero-weighted), so they raise record counts but add nothing to "
    f"any weighted sum.\n"
    f"- **Weighted trip and tour totals differ modestly** "
    f"({(new_trips['trexpfac'].sum() / leg_trips['trexpfac'].sum() - 1) * 100:+.1f}% trips, "
    f"{(new_tours['toexpfac'].sum() / leg_tours['toexpfac'].sum() - 1) * 100:+.1f}% tours) "
    f"because the two pipelines emit different trip/tour *sets* and the new pipeline derives "
    f"the tour weight as the mean of its linked-trip weights rather than inheriting the "
    f"person-day weight (@sec-divergences).\n"
    f"- Largest weighted-share gap: **{wp['share_delta'].abs().max():.1f} pp** (purpose), "
    f"**{wm['share_delta'].abs().max():.1f} pp** (mode)."
))
```

SCENARIOS = {

## 14. Divergences {#sec-divergences}

Two kinds of difference: **record-count** differences (which rows each pipeline emits,
decomposed in the record lineage of @sec-unweighted) and **column** differences (values
on the rows both emit, catalogued here). None is a data defect.

```{python}
#| label: divergences
#| echo: false

n_zero_pdays = new_pdays.filter(pl.col("pdexpfac") <= 0).height
display(Markdown(f"""
Every column flagged or marked non-comparable in @sec-coverage carries a documented
cause, catalogued below by category (from the divergence registry `spec.DIVERGENCES`).
The dominant record-count driver — the new pipeline keeping **{n_zero_pdays:,}** zero-weight
person-days legacy drops, offset by tour-formatting trip drops — is shown in the record
counts of @sec-unweighted.
"""))

_CATS = [
    ("unimplemented", "Unimplemented / stubbed"),
    ("id space", "Independent id space"),
    ("encoding", "Encoding convention"),
    ("spec mismatch", "Spec-vs-implementation"),
    ("weight", "Weighting"),
    ("config", "Config switch"),
]

def _category(note: str) -> str:
    low = note.lower()
    for key, label in _CATS:
        if key in low:
            return label
    return "Value difference"

rows = []
for table in ["hh", "person", "personday", "tour", "trip"]:
    for cs in S.columns(table):
        note = S.divergence(table, cs.name)
        if note:
            rows.append({"category": _category(note), "column": f"{table}.{cs.name}",
                         "cause": note})
order = {label: i for i, (_, label) in enumerate(_CATS)}
order["Value difference"] = len(_CATS)
div_tbl = (
    pl.DataFrame(rows)
    .with_columns(pl.col("category").replace_strict(order).alias("_o"))
    .sort(["_o", "column"]).drop("_o")
)
show(div_tbl)
display(Markdown(
    f"\n{div_tbl.height} columns with a documented cause, across "
    f"{div_tbl['category'].n_unique()} categories. Every ⚠-flagged column in "
    f"@sec-coverage appears here."
))
```

## 15. Robustness & configurability {#sec-config}

- **Schema validation at every step** — all canonical and DaySim/CT-RAMP outputs are
  Pydantic-validated (`src/data_canon/`); the legacy scripts validate nothing. This
  report reads that same schema, so it cannot drift out of sync with the pipeline.
- **Behaviour as configuration** — linking thresholds, partial-tour dropping, weighting
  source, imputation, income thresholds and the DaySim TAZ system are all config.
- **IDs preserved & richer output** — canonical IDs survive to every output; the fields
  legacy stubs out (`puwmode`, `ptpass`, `pproxy`, `ppaidprk`) are populated.
- **Per-step caching & tests** — content-hash caching, plus unit and end-to-end
  synthetic-data suites (`tests/e2e/`).
